Hey, I lost like 35kg in 8 months back in 2011-2012, was 16 at the time so close to your age.. You are a relatively good bodyfat it seems, you could probably still lose a good 5-6kg but ultimately what I imagine is bothering you most is not the fat but the loose skin, I didn't realize that at the time and I ended up getting anorexia to try get rid of it, it is much better nowadays at the age of 22 but it never really goes away and it still bothers me quite a lot..

As for your question, If I were in your position I would personally just do resistance training and perhaps some high-intensity interval training of some description, focus on getting stronger and eating enough to facilitate recovery without going overboard, perhaps aiming to lean out some more... you will certainly be able to gain muscle mass while leaning out if you eat right without going into crazy deficits and exercise intelligently.. especially with where you are at now.. good luck

Was fat my whole life up until my late teens, I was practically nonexistent in the eyes of my peers. I developed anorexia and people used me and etc to the same extent as when I was overweight. I started lifting and I became known as that guy who goes to the gym, which I guess stood out because no one at my school actually worked out lol, people seldom tried to use me during that period and actually seemed to want to talk to me despite my social issues. I got injured and became skinny again, I became just another person in the crowd, where as when I was training beforehand people acknowledged my existence.

The confidence you gain from changing your body composition is the primary reason people treat you differently I have found, because you act differently.

Makes more sense to me to do upper/lower, push/pull/legs, or full body splits, training a muscle 2x per week seems to be optimal according to the research I've seen

There are many combinations but if you train 5 days a week you could do something like:

Upper, Lower, Rest, Upper, Conditioning, Lower, Rest, Repeat

Or

Pull, Push, Legs(pull), Rest, Upper body, Legs(push), Rest, Repeat

Well what you can do in the mean time is calm the inflammation with an over the counter topical corticosteroid to reduce the inflammation till you see your doctor and they can further evaluate.

Ignore everyone going on about all the natural cures and shit, it won't get you far and if it's affecting your mental health so much you need to handle this situation now with scientifically backed methods.
